operational_record.cause_of_end: Faulty software command sent from Earth accidentally overwrote telemetry antenna pointing parameters
operational_record.historic_feat: First successful long-duration American landing and transmission of color images and in-situ biological tests from the Martian surface

science_instruments: Biology Experiment Package (Pyrolytic Release, Labeled Release, Gas Exchange)
Surface Sampler Collector Arm with backhoe trenching shovel

historic_discoveries.finding: Rapid release of radioactive 14-CO2 gas upon nutrient injection; originally debated as biological metabolism, later attributed to reactive perchlorates and superoxide radicals in soil
Did not detect ambient organic compounds down to parts-per-billion threshold; explained decades later by presence of oxidizing soil perchlorates that combusted organics during pyrolysis heating
historic_discoveries.status: Later corrected by Curiosity & Perseverance findings

historic_discoveries.finding: Surface atmospheric pressure varied cyclically between 6.8 and 9.0 mbar as polar CO2 caps froze and sublimated annually; temperatures ranged from -89°C to -17°C

astronaut_tactical_note: Chryse Planitia offers flat, wide landing terrain with abundant basaltic gravel. Atmospheric pressure is relatively high for Mars (~7.5 mbar), reducing rocket fuel requirements for powered descent. Beware reactive oxidizing soil chemistry.
